title: Court Orders State Department to Reopen 55,000-Visa Green Card Lottery
excerpt: A California federal judge ordered the State Department to reinstate the fiscal 2027 Diversity Visa lottery for up to 55,000 applicants, in a preliminary injunction in Red Eagle Law v. Rubio.
body:
• A federal judge in California has ordered the State Department to reinstate the fiscal 2027 Diversity Visa lottery, which makes up to 55,000 immigrant visas available each year to people from countries with historically low US immigration.
  • Judge Jinsook Ohta's October 14 preliminary injunction in Red Eagle Law LC v. Rubio required registration to open by October 18 and run through November 19; as of October 16, registration had not yet opened and no official dates had been announced.
  • Reader action: do not pay any third-party site — entry is only through the official dvprogram.state.gov portal, and check the State Department's DV-2027 page for the announced window before entering.
  • Winning entry is not a green card by itself: selectees must still meet education or work-experience eligibility, admissibility rules, and complete processing before September 30, 2027.

A federal judge has ordered the US State Department to restart the Diversity Visa lottery for fiscal 2027, restoring — at least for now — a program that offers permanent residence to up to 55,000 people a year from countries with historically lower levels of immigration to the United States.

Judge Jinsook Ohta of the US District Court for the Southern District of California issued a preliminary injunction on October 14 halting the program's suspension, according to Bloomberg Law. She said the lottery must be open by October 18, with registration lasting through November 19. Boundless, summarizing the ruling on October 16, said the order requires a registration window of at least 30 days, and noted that as of Friday morning registration had not opened and the State Department had not announced official dates.

How the lottery ended up in court

The Diversity Visa program, created by Congress in 1990, reserves visas for applicants from countries that send relatively few immigrants to the United States; many recipients in recent years have come from Africa, according to Bloomberg Law. The Trump administration suspended the program last December after a Portuguese national who had received a visa through the program was suspected of killing four people in two shootings in Rhode Island and Massachusetts and was later found dead by suicide. In March, the administration also issued a rule requiring applicants to hold a passport.

Red Eagle Law LC, a California immigration law firm, sued Secretary of State Marco Rubio seeking resumption of the program after the department failed to announce a registration period. Judge Ohta had earlier denied a temporary restraining order in the same case, Bloomberg Law reported. The case is Red Eagle Law LC v. Rubio, No. 3:26-cv-04738. The State Department told Bloomberg Law it would not comment on pending litigation.

The department's own DV-2027 notice, last updated November 5, 2025, said it was changing the entry process, would announce the registration start date as soon as practicable, and that the visa application period for selectees would remain October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027. That unchanged end date is what makes the delay consequential: every week without registration compresses selection and visa processing into the same fixed year.

What this means for applicants

For prospective entrants, including relatives of Indian and other diaspora families in eligible countries, the injunction matters only if the department actually opens the portal. India itself is generally not an eligible country because of high immigration volumes, so most India-born readers will not qualify directly, but spouses or parents born in eligible countries can sometimes provide an alternative country of chargeability under program rules — applicants should verify eligibility on the official instructions rather than through agents.

Three practical points follow from the sources. First, use only the official entry site, dvprogram.state.gov; the government does not notify winners by email or phone, and results are checked through Entrant Status Check with a confirmation number that must be saved. Second, prepare documents now — a valid passport is now required under the March rule reported by Bloomberg Law, and a compressed timeline leaves little room for corrections. Third, submit only one entry per person; duplicate entries void eligibility under program rules.

What happens next

The injunction is preliminary, not a final judgment, and the government can seek a stay from Judge Ohta or the Ninth Circuit. That legal risk, plus the State Department's silence as of October 16, means applicants should treat the October 18 opening date in Bloomberg Law's report as a court deadline to watch, not as a confirmed live portal. If registration opens, selectees must still complete the full visa process before September 30, 2027, or when the 55,000 visas are exhausted, whichever comes first.

Check the State Department page and official portal daily once an announcement appears, and avoid paid sites promising early registration.
